comparator.sourceNotes: The first-listed Jewish Studies and Hebrew major is followed consistently through years two and three; the separately listed English-taught Middle Eastern Studies major is not combined with it. Year one comprises eight 6-EC courses and one 12-EC humanities introduction (60 EC), including four Modern Hebrew language-acquisition modules and Biblical Hebrew. Year two has five 6-EC courses and a 30-EC Jewish Studies and Hebrew abroad semester (60 EC). Year three has three 6-EC courses, 30 EC genuine free choice and a compulsory 12-EC thesis (60 EC). The 30-EC abroad semester is retained as a named requirement without inventing host modules. The study guide identifies the bachelor as 180 EC and Dutch-taught; the published curriculum page establishes this selected major’s weights.

routeSelection.route: Major Joodse studies en Hebreeuws (Jewish Studies and Hebrew)
routeSelection.basis: The UvA presents two majors after the shared first year. Select the first-listed Jewish Studies and Hebrew major, which develops the degree’s Hebrew-language and Jewish-studies identity, under the official-order tie break. The Middle Eastern Studies major is a separate, broader route and is not used to make a more convenient UCR comparison.

exception.reason: The common first year requires Modern Hebrew Language Acquisition 1–4 and Biblical Hebrew; the selected major adds a 3000-year Hebrew prose-and-poetry sequence, an advanced Hebrew intensive, a 30-EC subject-linked study-abroad semester, Jewish history and thought, Bible source work and a field thesis. The UCR workbook has no Modern or Biblical Hebrew instruction, Hebrew-source reading sequence, or sustained Jewish-studies curriculum. A 24-course path in general literature, archaeology, philosophy, politics and international relations would displace the defining subject rather than credibly approximate it. Open electives cannot substitute for these compulsory components.
exception.curriculumContext: The first-listed route has 60 EC shared first year, 30 EC listed second-year taught courses plus 30 EC Jewish Studies and Hebrew abroad semester, and 18 EC listed third-year taught courses plus 30 EC genuine free choice and 12 EC thesis: exactly 180 EC. The separate Middle Eastern Studies major is mutually exclusive, not a pool of additional requirements.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works introduces Gilgamesh within a broad literary survey; MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature compares ancient epic traditions; MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology considers ancient Near Eastern material cultures among many other regions; GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy and GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations supply general disciplinary context. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean and MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning address Mediterranean culture or language in different contexts. None teaches Modern Hebrew, Biblical Hebrew, original Hebrew textual interpretation, sustained Jewish religious or intellectual history, or the subject-specific abroad work. These isolated adjacent courses do not support a coherent 24-course Hebrew and Jewish Studies programme.
